chunks: My father (rah) said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to me, raising it to Hisham ibn Salim, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the one who imprecates Ali (peace be upon him). He said: 'By Allah, he is halal al-damm (permissible to kill), were it not that it might cause an innocent person to be killed by him.' I asked: 'Which thing causes an innocent to be killed by him?' He said: 'A believer is killed in retaliation for an infidel.'

key_terms.حَلَالُ الدَّمِ: Permissible to kill (blood is lawful to shed)
key_terms.سَبَّابَهٌ: The one who imprecates or curses
key_terms.یَعُمَّ بِهِ بَرِیئاً: It causes an innocent to be killed (general retaliation)
key_terms.یُقْتَلُ مُؤْمِنٌ بِکَافِرٍ: A believer is killed in retaliation for an infidel

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on killing one who imprecates Imam Ali (a.s.) and what is the condition for suspending it?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.) establishes that cursing Imam Ali (a.s.) renders the perpetrator *halal al-damm* (permissible to kill), a ruling rooted in the severity of enmity toward the Imam. However, this is suspended under the principle of *qatl al-mu'min bi-l-kafir*, where killing the guilty party might inadvertently cause the death of an innocent believer through general retaliation or collective punishment. This highlights the Shia jurisprudential balance between upholding the status of the Imam and preserving the lives of the broader community.
